title: Rite transcript line (format 0, vocabulary 0)
description: One line of a transcript.jsonl file. The first line is the header; every other line records one fact, either complete or withheld. Each line is a JSON object on its own line, and the lines are chained: each line's chain value commits to the line and to every line before it.

ActId.description: An act's identifier, as written in the ceremony.

At.description: When the fact was recorded: an RFC 3339 time in UTC with six fractional digits. The chain commits to this exact string.

CompleteLine.description: A fact line with its content: the fact, the salt that hides it, and the values that commit to both.

chain.description: The chain value after this line: SHA-256 over the byte 0x01, the previous chain value, the length of `at` as an 8-byte big-endian integer, `at` in UTF-8, the level as an 8-byte big-endian integer, and the leaf. The chain value of the last line is the transcript's fingerprint.

leaf.description: The commitment to the fact: SHA-256 over the byte 0x00, the 16 salt bytes, and the fact in RFC 8785 canonical JSON.

salt.description: 16 random bytes, written as 32 lowercase hex digits. The leaf hashes the decoded bytes. The salt keeps a withheld fact from being guessed from its leaf.

ErrorClass.description: What kind of bad outcome this was.

oneOf.description: Something around the ceremony was not ready, such as a device not connected, and the step's work did not happen.
The ceremony's own logic concluded badly, such as a verification that did not match or a refused attestation.
The run itself cannot be trusted to continue, or the ceremony definition is broken.
An operator chose to stop the ceremony.

ErrorRecord.description: What went wrong: a class for audit, a stable kind, and a message for people.

class.description: The kind of bad outcome, for audit.

kind.description: A stable label for the error, such as aborted or step_failed.

message.description: A description of the error for people.

Format.description: What kind of value a person types.

oneOf.description: Anything the person can type.
Decimal digits only.
ASCII letters and digits.
Bytes as hexadecimal, in either case, two digits per byte.
Bytes as standard base64 with padding.

HeaderLine.description: The first line of a transcript: what the file is, and the start of the chain.

$schema.description: The URL of the JSON Schema of the release that wrote the transcript, for editors and other tools. The chain does not commit to it, and a reader ignores it.

chain.description: The first chain value: SHA-256 over the byte 0x02 followed by the header in RFC 8785 canonical JSON.

Level.description: The confidentiality level of a line: who may see its fact. Levels are integers ordered from the widest audience to the narrowest, so a disclosure up to a level withholds every line above it. Three levels are built in at fixed values: public (10, anyone), restricted (20, auditors under agreement) and confidential (30, the ceremony's own organisation). Every level a transcript uses is declared in its header.

MaterialId.description: A material's identifier, as written in the ceremony.

ParamId.description: A parameter's identifier, as written in the ceremony.

Prompt.description: A prompt as it was shown.

oneOf.description: A yes or no question.

default.description: The answer given when the person confirms without choosing, if any.

oneOf.description: A request for free text, checked before it is accepted.

validator.description: The check the answer had to pass.

oneOf.description: A request for a secret, such as a PIN. The answer is never recorded.

validator.description: The check the answer had to pass.

oneOf.description: A request to type a given text exactly, such as a confirmation phrase.

expected.description: The text that had to be typed.

oneOf.description: A pause until the person is ready to continue.

ResponseRecord.description: The answer to a prompt, as recorded. A secret answer is never recorded, not even as a digest.

oneOf.description: A yes or no answer.
A free-text answer.
A secret was entered. Only the fact that it was entered is recorded.
The person continued past a pause.

RoleId.description: A role's identifier, as written in the ceremony.

Sha256Digest.description: A SHA-256 digest: `sha256:` followed by 64 lowercase hex digits.

StepFact.description: One recorded fact, identified by its `type`. Each fact type has a fixed set of fields in a given vocabulary.

oneOf.description: The ceremony started.

template.description: Digest of the ceremony definition file the run was resolved from. The inputs of the run are recorded as their own facts, so this digest covers the definition only.

oneOf.description: A role the ceremony defines. Recorded once per role at the start, whether or not anyone is assigned to it; later facts name the role by its identifier.
A person was assigned to a role for this run. One fact per assignment, so each can be withheld on its own.

person.description: The person, as supplied when the run started. Recorded as given: nothing in the transcript proves who the person is.

oneOf.description: A parameter took its value for this run, supplied or defaulted.

value.description: The value, as the ceremony used it.

oneOf.description: A material was loaded at the start of the run. The digest of a digital material is a separate fact, material_digest, so the two can be disclosed to different audiences.

identifier.description: The identifier of a physical or pre-provisioned material, such as a serial number, when one was supplied.

oneOf.description: The digest of a digital material's bytes, as loaded.

digest.description: The digest of the material's bytes.

oneOf.description: A backend was used for the first time in this run. Recorded once per backend, before its first operation; operations name the backend and do not repeat its identity.

identity.description: The identity the backend reports for itself, such as a device serial number and firmware version.

name.description: The backend's name in the ceremony.

provider.description: The kind of backend, such as openssl, yubikey or pkcs11.

oneOf.description: A description of the machine the ceremony ran on.

info.description: The parts of the machine description the step was asked to record.

oneOf.description: An act, a named part of the ceremony, started.

label.description: The act's label, as written in the ceremony.

oneOf.description: A step started.

label.description: The step's label, as written in the ceremony.

role.description: The role responsible for the step. Its display name is on the role's role_declared fact.

oneOf.description: Someone answered a prompt, and the answer was accepted.

step.description: The step that asked, or absent for a prompt asked outside any step.

oneOf.description: A backend performed an operation. The inputs and outputs are specific to the kind of operation.

backend.description: The backend the step ran with, by the name the ceremony gives it.                 Its identity is on that backend's backend_bound fact. Absent for an operation                 done in software.

fingerprint.description: A fingerprint of the material the operation produced, when it has one.

inputs.description: What the operation was given: parameters and references to artifacts or materials.

kind.description: The kind of operation, such as generate_key or sign_data.

outputs.description: What the operation produced: artifact names and digests.

step.description: The step the operation ran in.

oneOf.description: A key held outside the ceremony received a wrapped key. A separate fact from the operation, so the method of a wrap can be published while the recipient stays withheld.

declared.description: Whether the ceremony named this fingerprint in advance. When it did, the key received was checked against it; otherwise the fingerprint records whatever key arrived.

fingerprint.description: The digest of the recipient's public key, as DER-encoded SubjectPublicKeyInfo.

source.description: The artifact or material the recipient's key came from, by its name in the ceremony.

step.description: The step that wrapped the key.

oneOf.description: A person made an attestation.

role.description: The role that made the attestation.

step.description: The step the attestation was made in.

oneOf.description: An artifact was written to the run's artifacts directory.

digest.description: The digest of the file's bytes. Absent for content a step opened, since a digest of a secret can be tested against guesses.

file.description: The file name in the artifacts directory: a single path component.

name.description: The artifact's name, as declared in the ceremony.

step.description: The step that produced the artifact.

oneOf.description: An operator recorded a deviation.

step.description: The step during which the deviation was recorded, or absent outside any step.

oneOf.description: One attempt at a step failed. Recorded per attempt: a step that is retried and then succeeds has this fact for each failed attempt, then step_completed.

attempt.description: The attempt's number within the step, starting at 1.

error.description: What went wrong in this attempt.

oneOf.description: A step finished.
The ceremony finished. It is the last line of a transcript whose run completed.
The ceremony failed or was aborted. It is the last line of a transcript whose run did not complete.
The ceremony's entropy source was seeded with machine randomness. Recorded once, at the start, so every value drawn from the source can be derived again from the transcript.

derivation.description: The derivation scheme, such as rite-kdf/v1. A verifier refuses a scheme it does not know.

m.description: The machine randomness, as lowercase hex.

source.description: Where the machine randomness came from, such as os.

oneOf.description: A person added their own randomness to the entropy source, starting a new epoch.

contribution.description: The contribution, word for word, mixed into the source as UTF-8.

epoch.description: The epoch this contribution starts, counting from 1.

step.description: The step the contribution was made in.

oneOf.description: A value was drawn from the entropy source, such as a nonce, a certificate serial number or a challenge. A verifier derives it again from the seed, the contributions and the path.

step.description: The step that drew the value.

value.description: The value, as lowercase hex. Its length is the number of bytes drawn.

StepId.description: A step's identifier, as written in the ceremony.

oneOf.description: The step did its work.

message.description: A short description of what the step did.

TranscriptHeader.description: What the file is. A reader checks `rite_transcript` before reading anything else, and refuses a version it does not know.

dry_run.description: Whether the run was a dry run. A dry-run transcript is a rehearsal record, never evidence of a ceremony.

levels.description: Every level the transcript uses, by name. It holds public, restricted and confidential at their fixed values, and any other level the ceremony declares. No two names share a value.

producer.description: The program and version that wrote the transcript, as it reports itself. Informational: a program cannot vouch for its own identity.

rite_transcript.description: Version of the line format and the chain rule.

run_id.description: A random identifier of this run: 32 lowercase hex digits.

vocabulary.description: Version of the fact vocabulary: which fact types and fields the transcript uses.

ValidatorSpec.description: The check an answer had to pass.

oneOf.description: The answer is not empty or blank.
The answer matches a regular expression in full.
The answer passes a check the program defines, by name.

value.description: The name of the check, such as serial_number.

oneOf.description: The answer is a value of one format, with a length within bounds, counted in characters for text and in bytes for an encoding.

format.description: What kind of value the answer is.

max_length.description: The most units accepted, if bounded.

min_length.description: The fewest units accepted, if bounded.

WithheldLine.description: A fact line whose fact is withheld from a disclosure. It keeps the time, the level, the leaf and the chain value, so it folds into the chain exactly as the complete line does, and the transcript keeps its fingerprint.

chain.description: The chain value after this line.

leaf.description: The commitment to the withheld fact.
